caption: Figure 2: PaLM-540B prompting results with respect to number of CoT-SC samples used.
description:
This figure is a line graph showing the performance of PaLM-540B prompting with respect to the number of CoT-SC samples used. The graph has four series: red, blue, green, and orange. The blue series is the highest, reaching approximately 34, while the red series is the lowest, staying around 28. The graph shows an increasing trend for all series as the number of CoT-SC samples increases.

caption: Figure 3: Scaling results for prompting and finetuning on HotPotQA with ReAct (ours) and baselines.
description:
## Index Section 1
Figure: Bar chart comparing performance of different methods on HotPotQA for prompt learning and fine-tuning. Two panels show results for 8b, 62b, and 540b model sizes. Highest performance is achieved by ReAct for fine-tuning at 540b size, with an EM score of around 32. Lowest performance is Standard method for prompt learning at 8b size, with an EM score of around 15.

caption: Figure 4: Another example HotpotQA question, where the original label is outdated. Only ReAct is able to obtain the up-to-date answer thanks to real-world web interaction plus reasoning.
description:
Figure type: Text-based comparison of two models' performance on a HotpotQA question.
Content: The figure compares the performance of two models, Standard and ReAct, on a HotpotQA question about the number of rooms in a hotel. The original label is outdated. The ReAct model is able to obtain the up-to-date answer thanks to real-world web interaction plus reasoning.

Search index sections:
- "ReAct model obtains up-to-date answer for HotpotQA question"
- "Standard model fails to find correct answer for outdated HotpotQA question"

caption: Figure 5: A human-in-the-loop behavior correction example with ReAct in AlfWorld. (a) ReAct trajectory fails due to a hallucinating thought (Act 17). (b) By a human simply editing two thoughts (Act 17, 23), the ReAct trajectory produces desirable reasoning traces and actions and succeeds.
description:
Figure type: Diagram
Description: The figure shows two panels, labeled (a) ReAct and (b) ReAct (Human Thought edit). Panel (a) depicts a failed trajectory due to a hallucinating thought, while panel (b) shows a corrected trajectory after human intervention. The human edited two thoughts (Act 17, 23), leading to successful reasoning and actions.

Text in figure: 
- Panel (a) ReAct: Observations 16-26, Actions 16-29, Thoughts 17, 23
- Panel (b) ReAct (Human Thought edit): Observations 16-29, Actions 16-29, Thoughts 17, 23, 25, 26
